title: 希腊悲剧的起源、结构与情感净化
topic: The origins and structure of Greek tragedy, and its contrast with comedy

sentences.en: Western theater really begins with the tragedy of ancient Athens, a form that grew out of festivals honoring the god Dionysus, where singers likely began with improvisation before fixed texts existed.
sentences.zh: 西方戏剧真正始于古代雅典的悲剧，这种形式脱胎于祭祀酒神狄俄尼索斯的节庆；在固定文本出现之前，歌者很可能是从即兴表演开始的。

sentences.en: At those festivals, playwrights competed against one another, each submitting a script, and a playwright often served as his own director, training the performers himself.
sentences.zh: 在那些节庆上，剧作家们彼此竞演，各自提交一部剧本，而剧作家往往还兼任自己剧目的导演，亲自训练表演者。

sentences.en: The most striking feature of early drama was the chorus, a group who sang and danced together, commenting on the action and voicing the reaction of the community.
sentences.zh: 早期戏剧最鲜明的特征是歌队，一群人一起歌唱、舞蹈，对剧情加以评述，并道出整个共同体的反应。

sentences.en: For a long time there was only the chorus and one actor; then Aeschylus added a second and Sophocles a third, which finally made real dialogue between characters possible.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里舞台上只有歌队和一名演员；后来埃斯库罗斯加入第二名、索福克勒斯加入第三名，这才让角色之间真正的对话成为可能。

sentences.en: A Greek tragedy usually centers on a protagonist of high rank, opposed by an antagonist or hostile force, and the clash between them drives the whole plot forward.
sentences.zh: 一部希腊悲剧通常围绕一位地位崇高的主角展开，与他对立的是一个反派或某种敌对力量，两者的冲突推动着整个情节向前。

sentences.en: The hero typically falls because of a single fatal flaw, and as the tension rises to its climax, he recognizes his mistake too late.
sentences.zh: 主角通常因某个致命缺陷而败亡；当张力升至高潮，他认清错误时却已为时太晚。

sentences.en: From this Aristotle drew his famous idea of catharsis, the emotional release the audience feels after being moved to pity and fear, as if watching a noble figure suffer could cleanse the spectators.
sentences.zh: 由此亚里士多德提出了他著名的“catharsis”（情感宣泄）概念：观众在被激起怜悯与恐惧后所感到的释放，仿佛观看一位高贵人物受难便能涤净观者的心灵。

sentences.en: Comedy, the great counterpart to tragedy, aimed for the opposite effect: it usually ends happily, often with a marriage, and it relies on irony, the gap between what characters believe and what is true.
sentences.zh: 喜剧作为悲剧伟大的对应体，追求相反的效果：它通常以圆满收场，常以婚礼告终，并依赖反讽——即角色所信与真相之间的落差。

sentences.en: Aristophanes pushed this into satire, mocking real politicians on the public stage, while a wilder kind of comedy, the farce, piled up absurd coincidences purely to make the crowd laugh.
sentences.zh: 阿里斯托芬把这一手法推向讽刺，在公共舞台上嘲弄真实的政客；而一种更狂野的喜剧——闹剧，则堆叠荒诞的巧合，纯粹为逗乐观众。

sentences.en: In performance, a full play was divided into large sections we call an act, and within each act a change of place or time marked a new scene.
sentences.zh: 在演出中，一整部戏被划分为若干称作“一幕”的大段，而在每一幕之内，地点或时间的变换就标示出新的一场。

sentences.en: Long before opening night, the cast would gather for rehearsal, walking through their lines until the timing felt natural.
sentences.zh: 远在首演之夜前，全体演员就会聚在一起排练，把台词反复走一遍，直到节奏变得自然。

sentences.en: Actors wore large masks and stylized costumes so the audience could read a character from a distance, and they used few props, though every object that appeared, a sword or an urn, carried real weight.
sentences.zh: 演员戴着巨大的面具、穿着风格化的戏装，好让观众能从远处辨认出角色；他们用的道具很少，但每一件出现的物件——一把剑或一只骨灰瓮——都承载着实实在在的分量。

sentences.en: One key technique is the soliloquy, in which a character alone on stage reveals his private thoughts aloud, unlike a plain monologue, which is simply one person speaking at length to others.
sentences.zh: 一种关键手法是独白，即角色独自站在台上把内心想法出声袒露；这不同于单纯的长段独说，后者只是一个人对着别人长篇讲话。

sentences.en: Centuries later Shakespeare inherited all of this and made the soliloquy the heart of his tragedies, most famously in Hamlet's "To be, or not to be."
sentences.zh: 数百年后莎士比亚继承了这一切，把独白变成他悲剧的核心，最著名的便是哈姆雷特那句“生存，还是毁灭”。

sentences.en: So when you sit as a spectator, remember that this dramatic form is one of humanity's oldest inventions for making sense of suffering, and it still works on us today.
sentences.zh: 所以当你作为一名观众坐着看戏时，请记住：这种戏剧形式是人类为理解苦难而发明的最古老形式之一，而它至今仍在打动我们。
